title: DARIS: An Oversubscribed Spatio-Temporal Scheduler for Real-Time DNN Inference on GPUs
problem: GPUs face underutilization in DNN inference workloads due to coarse-grained scheduling that cannot exploit fine-grained spatial and temporal concurrency.
motivation: Real-time DNN inference demands require meeting deadlines while maximizing GPU utilization in edge and inference-focused deployments.
method: DARIS is a scheduler that decides what work runs on a GPU when. It combines two techniques: NVIDIA's Multi-Process Service (MPS) lets multiple tasks share different parts of the same GPU at the same time (space-sharing), while CUDA streams run tasks at different times in sequence (time-sharing). The system synchronizes these tasks so work can move between GPU sections instantly without waiting. By analyzing how tasks can run concurrently, it packs more work onto the GPU than conventional approaches allow.
key_novelty: The core insight is combining GPU space-sharing (via MPS) and time-sharing (via CUDA streams) with zero-delay work migration, which lets you run more real-time neural network tasks on one GPU than standard scheduling methods.
contributions: All high-priority tasks meet deadlines; low-priority miss rate under 2%
33% better high-priority response times vs low-priority tasks
limitations: Evaluation primarily on GPUs; generalization to other accelerators not discussed.
primary_theme: Oversubscribed spatio-temporal scheduling for real-time DNN inference
